q: All of the following cause chronic diarrhoea EXCEPT:
A 2-year-old has passed loose stools containing undigested vegetables 4 times a day for months; he drinks a lot of juice and grows normally. What is the diagnosis?
e: Chronic non-specific (toddler's) diarrhoea: normal growth, undigested food in the stool and excess fruit juice.

q: The best screening test for coeliac disease is:
e: tTG-IgA is the best test; total IgA is measured to exclude IgA deficiency.

q: Regarding coeliac disease, all are true EXCEPT:
o: It is a T-cell reaction to gluten
Treatment is a lifelong gluten-free diet
It may present with short stature
It is linked with Down syndrome
e: Rice and maize are free of gluten and safe.

q: Biopsy findings of coeliac disease include all EXCEPT:
A teenager has weight loss, short stature, abdominal pain and a perianal fistula. The most likely diagnosis is:
e: Perianal disease, growth failure and transmural fistulas are typical of Crohn disease.

q: After rotavirus gastroenteritis, a baby has frothy acidic stools and sore buttocks. What is the best management?
o: Continue breastfeeding; a lactose-free formula if formula-fed
e: Secondary lactose intolerance is temporary; breastfeeding continues.

q: A 13-month-old has had chronic diarrhoea since 3 months of age, with failure to thrive; the stools contain reducing sugars and no pathogens. What is the most likely diagnosis?
e: Onset at 3 months on milk feeds, with damaged mucosa, fits cow's milk protein enteropathy; coeliac disease needs wheat, which is introduced after 6 months.

q: The formula of choice for a formula-fed infant with cow's milk protein allergy is:
e: Lactose-free formula still contains cow's milk protein, so an extensively hydrolysed formula is used.

q: What is the IMCI management of persistent diarrhoea with some dehydration?
e: Severe persistent diarrhoea (with any dehydration) is treated for dehydration and referred.
